name: Quadratic Chabauty
function_signature: (Curve C/ℚ with Mordell-Weil rank = genus) → (Finite locus containing C(ℚ))
description: The depth-two explicit instance of Kim's nonabelian Chabauty method (Balakrishnan-Dogra) that uses p-adic height pairings to cut out an explicit finite locus containing the rational points when the Mordell-Weil rank equals the genus.
_source: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Kim's Nonabelian Chabauty Method
function_signature: (Curve C/ℚ, unipotent fundamental group data) → (Selmer-type p-adic locus containing C(ℚ))
description: A generalization of Chabauty's method replacing the Jacobian by the unipotent (de Rham/étale) fundamental group, locating rational points inside a Selmer-type p-adic locus cut out by iterated Coleman integrals.
_source: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Coleman's Effective Chabauty Bound
description: Under the Chabauty rank hypothesis, a curve of genus g with good reduction at a prime p > 2g has at most #C(𝔽_p) + 2g − 2 rational points.
_source: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Lawrence-Venkatesh Method
function_signature: (Family of curves over a base, p-adic Hodge data) → (Finiteness of rational points)
description: A proof of the Mordell conjecture using a Kodaira-Parshin family of covers and p-adic Hodge theory to show that the p-adic Galois representations attached to fibers vary so much that only finitely many fibers sit over rational points.
_source: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Skolem's Method (p-adic, integral points)
function_signature: (Integral-point equation) → (Finite set of integral solutions)
description: A p-adic method for integral points expressing solutions as zeros of p-adic analytic functions whose finiteness follows from the Strassmann/Weierstrass preparation property of convergent p-adic power series.
_source: A p-adic approach to rational points on curves, Bjorn Poonen, 2021

name: Croot-Lev-Pach lemma
description: A low-degree multilinear polynomial that vanishes off the diagonal of a finite-field cube has a number of nonzero diagonal entries bounded by twice the dimension of the relevant low-degree polynomial space.
_source: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Ellenberg-Gijswijt cap set theorem
description: Every cap set in (ℤ/3ℤ)^n has size at most c^n with c ≈ 2.756, i.e. exponentially smaller than 3^n, resolving the cap set problem via the polynomial method.
_source: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Slice rank of a tensor
description: The minimum number of terms needed to write a tensor as a sum of products each of which depends in one factor on a single variable group and in the other on the rest (Tao's symmetric generalization of matrix rank).
_source: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Slice rank polynomial method
function_signature: (Combinatorial configuration as diagonal tensor) → (Exponential upper bound on its size)
description: A proof technique that bounds the size of a combinatorial configuration by encoding it as a tensor supported on a diagonal, bounding its slice rank from below by the support size and from above via low-degree polynomials.
_source: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Sunflower-free / tri-colored sum-free bounds via slice rank
description: Application of the slice rank method giving exponential upper bounds on sunflower-free set systems and on tri-colored sum-free sets in abelian groups (Naslund-Sawin, Blasiak et al.).
_source: New applications of the polynomial method: the cap set conjecture and beyond, Joshua A. Grochow, 2019

name: Analytic L-function (axiomatic)
description: A Dirichlet series with Euler product, meromorphic continuation, and a functional equation relating s to 1−s, packaged with prescribed analytic data such as conductor, gamma factors, and central character.
_source: Analytic L-functions: definitions, theorems, and connections, Farmer, Pitale, Ryan, and Schmidt, 2019

name: Stably Rational Variety
description: A variety X such that X × ℙ^m is rational for some m, an intermediate notion strictly between rational and unirational.
_source: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Lüroth Problem
description: The question of whether every unirational variety is rational, answered affirmatively for curves and surfaces but negatively in dimension three and higher.
_source: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Decomposition of the Diagonal Method
function_signature: (Variety X, specialization family) → (Obstruction certifying non-stable-rationality)
description: An obstruction to (stable) rationality showing that a stably rational variety admits a Chow-theoretic decomposition of its diagonal, whose failure under specialization (Voisin, Colliot-Thélène-Pirutka) certifies non-stable-rationality.
_source: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Non-Stable-Rationality of Very General Hypersurfaces
description: A very general hypersurface of sufficiently high degree in projective space (degree at least roughly two-thirds the dimension, after Totaro and Schreieder) is not stably rational.
_source: Algebraic hypersurfaces, Janos Kollar, 2019

name: Big Polynomial Ring / Uniformity (Erman-Sam-Snowden)
description: The phenomenon, formalized via the inverse-limit polynomial ring in infinitely many variables and GL-equivariant commutative algebra, that bounds on invariants of cubic (and higher-degree) forms become independent of the number of variables.
_source: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Stillman's Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The projective dimension of an ideal generated by a fixed number of homogeneous polynomials of fixed degrees is bounded independently of the number of variables of the ambient polynomial ring.
_source: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Strength of a Polynomial
description: The least number r such that a homogeneous form is a sum of r products of lower-degree forms, a measure of degeneracy controlling the uniform algebraic behavior of higher-degree forms.
_source: Cubics in 10 variables vs. cubics in 1000 variables: uniformity phenomena, Erman, Sam, and Snowden, 2019

name: Tangent Developable Surface
description: The ruled surface swept out by the tangent lines to a space curve, naturally attached to the curve and whose singular structure encodes the curve's projective geometry.
_source: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Green's Conjecture
description: The Clifford index of a smooth projective curve equals the index of the first nonzero linear syzygy in the minimal free resolution of its canonical embedding, proved generically by Voisin and in general via degenerations to tangent developable surfaces.
_source: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Koszul Cohomology / Property N_p
description: The graded groups computing the syzygies of an embedded variety, with property N_p meaning the resolution is linear up to homological degree p, governing how a curve is cut out by quadrics and higher relations.
_source: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Degeneration to Tangent Developable Surfaces
function_signature: (Canonical curve, specialization to tangent developable of rational normal curve) → (Computation of syzygies)
description: A proof method computing syzygies of canonical curves by specializing to the tangent developable of a rational normal curve and using its explicit, computable resolution.
_source: Tangent developable surfaces and the equations defining algebraic curves, Ein and Lazarsfeld, 2020

name: Compactified Jacobian / Universal Picard Variety
description: A compactification of the moduli of line bundles over a family of curves (including degenerate nodal fibers) parametrizing rank-one torsion-free sheaves with a stability condition.
_source: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Tropical / Dual-Graph Combinatorics of the Boundary
function_signature: (Boundary strata of a compactified moduli space) → (Polyhedral / tropical combinatorial encoding)
description: The encoding of the boundary strata of compactified moduli spaces by the dual graphs of stable curves, linking the geometry to tropical moduli and combinatorial polyhedral data.
_source: Compactifying moduli spaces, Lucia Caporaso, 2020

name: Space of Diagonal Harmonics
description: The bigraded vector space DH_n of polynomials in two sets of n variables killed by all symmetric-group-invariant differential operators of positive degree, carrying a diagonal S_n-action.
_source: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Nabla Operator
description: The Garsia-Bergeron linear operator on symmetric functions, diagonal in the modified Macdonald polynomial basis with explicit eigenvalues, whose value on e_n equals the bigraded Frobenius characteristic of diagonal harmonics.
_source: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Parking Function (combinatorics)
description: A Dyck path of order n together with a column-increasing labeling of its north steps by 1,...,n, equipped with the statistics area and dinv (diagonal inversions).
_source: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Shuffle Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The symmetric function ∇(e_n) equals the weighted generating function over parking functions of order n with weight q^dinv t^area times the quasisymmetric function of the descent set.
_source: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Compositional Shuffle Conjecture (Theorem)
description: A refinement of the shuffle conjecture indexed by compositions controlling the touch points of the Dyck path, whose proof by Carlsson and Mellit (via the double affine Hecke algebra) implies the shuffle conjecture.
_source: The shuffle conjecture, Stephanie van Willigenburg, 2020

name: Overconvergent Modular Form
description: A p-adic modular form converging on a strict neighborhood of the ordinary locus of the modular curve, organized into Coleman's finite-slope eigenvariety theory.
_source: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: U_p Operator and Slope Decomposition
description: The completely continuous Atkin-Lehner operator on spaces of overconvergent forms whose finite-slope generalized eigenspaces (by p-adic valuation of eigenvalue) give the finite-slope classical and overconvergent forms.
_source: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Coleman Classicality Theorem
description: An overconvergent eigenform of weight k and slope strictly less than k−1 is a classical modular form.
_source: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Rigid Meromorphic Cocycles / p-adic Singular Moduli
description: The Darmon-Vonk p-adic analogues of singular moduli, constructed from overconvergent forms and real quadratic geodesics, conjecturally algebraic and refining complex multiplication to real quadratic fields.
_source: Overconvergent modular forms and their explicit arithmetic, Jan Vonk, 2021

name: Classical Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity expressing a special value of a Siegel Eisenstein series as the average over a genus of theta series of quadratic forms.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Special Cycles on Shimura Varieties
description: Algebraic cycles on orthogonal or unitary Shimura varieties indexed by positive-definite quadratic/Hermitian data, generalizing Heegner points to higher codimension.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Kudla's Modularity Conjecture (Theorem)
description: The generating series whose coefficients are the classes of special cycles of a fixed codimension in the Chow group of a Shimura variety is a (vector-valued) modular form.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Geometric Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity expressing the special value of a Siegel Eisenstein series as a generating series of degrees/volumes of special cycles on a Shimura variety, lifting the classical formula to geometry.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil Formula
description: An identity relating arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on integral models of Shimura varieties to derivatives of Siegel Eisenstein series at the near-central point.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Kudla-Rapoport Conjecture (Theorem)
description: A local identity equating the arithmetic intersection number of special cycles on a Rapoport-Zink space with the derivative of a local representation/Whittaker density, proved by Li and Zhang.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Rapoport-Zink Space
description: A formal/rigid moduli space of p-divisible groups with additional structure (polarization, level) serving as the local p-adic uniformization of Shimura varieties.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Arithmetic Inner Product Formula
description: An identity relating the Beilinson-Bloch height of an arithmetic theta lift cycle to the central derivative of an L-function, generalizing the Gross-Zagier formula to higher dimension.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Beilinson-Bloch Conjecture
description: The conjecture that the rank of the Chow group of homologically trivial cycles on a smooth projective variety equals the order of vanishing of the associated L-function at the central point.
_source: From sum of two squares to arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas, Chao Li, 2023

name: Macaulay Inverse System
function_signature: (Artinian quotient of polynomial ring) ↔ (Finitely generated submodule of dual divided-power module)
description: Macaulay's duality between Artinian quotients of a polynomial ring and finitely generated submodules of the dual divided-power (or polynomial) module under contraction, parametrizing such quotients by inverse systems.
_source: F. S. Macaulay: from plane curves to Gorenstein rings, Eisenbud and Gray, 2023

name: Embedding Q into a Finitely Presented Group (Theorem)
description: The additive group of rational numbers embeds into a finitely presented group, realized via Belk-Hyde-Matucci using twisted Brin-Thompson groups acting on Cantor space.
_source: Embedding Q into a finitely presented group, Belk, Hyde, and Matucci, 2022

name: Twisted Brin-Thompson Group
description: A group of homeomorphisms of a Cantor space built from a base group acting on an alphabet together with prefix-replacement (Thompson-type) moves, simple and finitely presented under mild hypotheses.
_source: Embedding Q into a finitely presented group, Belk, Hyde, and Matucci, 2022

name: Space-time white noise
description: A Gaussian generalized random field on ℝ₊ × ℝ^d whose values over disjoint space-time regions are independent with covariance equal to the Lebesgue measure of their overlap.
_source: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Corwin and Shen, 2020

name: Dynamical Phi^4 equation
description: The renormalized stochastic reaction-diffusion equation ∂_t Φ = ΔΦ − (Φ³ − ∞·Φ) + ξ, the Langevin dynamics of Φ⁴ Euclidean QFT, singular in spatial dimension d = 2, 3.
_source: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Corwin and Shen, 2020

name: Parabolic Anderson Model
description: The linear singular SPDE ∂_t u = Δu + u·(ζ − ∞) with spatial white noise potential ζ, requiring renormalization in dimension d ≥ 2.
_source: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Corwin and Shen, 2020

name: Renormalization (counter-term subtraction) for singular SPDEs
function_signature: (Mollified singular SPDE) → (Nontrivial renormalized limit solution)
description: Mollifying the noise, subtracting divergent counter-terms C_ε (chosen via Gaussian moment / Wick-power computations) from the nonlinearity, and passing to the limit to obtain a nontrivial solution.
_source: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Corwin and Shen, 2020

name: Da Prato-Debussche trick
function_signature: (Not-too-singular SPDE) → (Well-posed fixed-point equation for the remainder)
description: Splitting the solution Φ = u + v into the stochastic linear (Gaussian) part u and a higher-regularity remainder v solving a classically well-posed fixed-point equation, valid for mildly singular equations such as 2D Φ⁴.
_source: Some recent progress in singular stochastic PDEs, Corwin and Shen, 2020

name: Primary uncertainty principle
description: For operators A, B with ‖A‖_{1→∞} ≤ 1, ‖B‖_{1→∞} ≤ 1 and ‖BAv‖_∞ ≥ k‖v‖_∞, one has ‖v‖₁‖Av‖₁ ≥ k‖v‖_∞‖Av‖_∞, from which classical Fourier uncertainty principles follow.
_source: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Wigderson and Wigderson, 2021

name: k-Hadamard matrix
description: A matrix A with entries bounded by 1 satisfying ‖A*Av‖_∞ ≥ k‖v‖_∞ (equivalently A*A invertible with ‖(A*A)⁻¹‖_{∞→∞} ≤ 1/k); precisely the matrices to which the primary uncertainty principle applies.
_source: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Wigderson and Wigderson, 2021

name: Donoho-Stark support-size uncertainty principle
description: For a nonzero function f on a finite abelian group G with Fourier transform f̂, the supports satisfy |supp(f)|·|supp(f̂)| ≥ |G|.
_deps: Fourier transform on finite abelian groups
_source: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Wigderson and Wigderson, 2021

name: Meshulam's non-abelian uncertainty principle
description: An extension of the Donoho-Stark support-size inequality to functions on arbitrary finite groups via rank and min-support notions of support for the Fourier transform.
_source: The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme, Wigderson and Wigderson, 2021

name: Hardy's uncertainty principle
description: If |f(x)| ≤ C e^{−a|x|²} and |f̂(ξ)| ≤ C e^{−b|ξ|²} with ab > 1/4 then f = 0, and with ab = 1/4 then f is a constant multiple of the Gaussian e^{−a|x|²}.
_source: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle, Fernandez-Bertolin and Malinnikova, 2021

name: Dynamical (Schrödinger) reformulation of Hardy's uncertainty principle
description: The reinterpretation of Hardy's theorem as a unique-continuation/rigidity statement for the free Schrödinger equation: a solution Gaussian-bounded at two distinct times must vanish.
_source: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle, Fernandez-Bertolin and Malinnikova, 2021

name: Liouville-theorem proof of Hardy's uncertainty principle
function_signature: (Schrödinger connection + bounded entire function) → (Hardy uncertainty rigidity)
description: A proof deriving the uncertainty principle from the Schrödinger connection together with Liouville's theorem for bounded entire functions rather than Phragmén-Lindelöf.
_deps: Dynamical (Schrödinger) reformulation of Hardy's uncertainty principle
_source: Dynamical versions of Hardy's uncertainty principle, Fernandez-Bertolin and Malinnikova, 2021

name: Sine-kernel Fredholm determinant
description: The determinant P_x = det(1 − K_sine) of the trace-class operator with kernel sin(x(z−z'))/(π(z−z')), giving the probability of no GUE eigenvalues in a union of bulk intervals.
_source: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Corwin, Deift and Its, 2022

name: Widom's large-gap asymptotics for the sine-kernel determinant
description: Widom's rigorous proof that ln P_x = −(x²/2)(1 + o(1)) as x → ∞, the first rigorous large-gap asymptotics for the sine determinant.
_source: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Corwin, Deift and Its, 2022

name: Tracy-Widom Painlevé representation
description: The identity F_2(t) = exp(−∫_t^∞ (s−t)u(s)² ds) where u is the Hastings-McLeod solution of the second Painlevé equation u_tt = t u + 2u³, with F_1, F_4 also expressed through u.
_source: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Corwin, Deift and Its, 2022

name: Integrable Fredholm operator
description: An integral operator whose kernel has the form (φ(z)ψ(z')−ψ(z)φ(z'))/(z−z'), a structure whose determinant satisfies nonlinear integrable PDEs and admits a Riemann-Hilbert representation.
_source: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Corwin, Deift and Its, 2022

name: Riemann-Hilbert / nonlinear steepest descent method
function_signature: (Painlevé / integrable-determinant function as RH problem) → (Asymptotics and connection formulae)
description: Representing Painlevé and integrable-determinant functions as matrix Riemann-Hilbert problems whose asymptotics are computed via the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent deformation of contours.
_source: Harold Widom's work in random matrix theory, Corwin, Deift and Its, 2022

name: Arnold's geodesic formulation of ideal hydrodynamics
description: The principle that the incompressible Euler equations are the geodesic equations of the right-invariant L² (kinetic-energy) metric on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.
_source: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Khesin, Misiolek and Modin, 2021

name: Newton's equations on diffeomorphism groups and density spaces
description: The generalization ∇_{q̇} q̇ = −∇U(q) of geodesic flow to infinite dimensions, with a potential U on Diff(M) or Dens(M), unifying compressible/incompressible fluids, MHD, shallow-water and relativistic fluid equations.
_deps: Arnold's geodesic formulation of ideal hydrodynamics
_source: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Khesin, Misiolek and Modin, 2021

name: Fisher-Rao information metric (infinite-dimensional)
description: The diffeomorphism-invariant information-geometric Riemannian metric on probability densities, whose Newton equations yield the μ-Camassa-Holm and Klein-Gordon type equations.
_source: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Khesin, Misiolek and Modin, 2021

name: Madelung transform as a symplectomorphism
description: The map sending a wave function to its density-and-phase (hydrodynamic) variables is a symplectomorphism (and Kähler morphism) intertwining the Schrödinger equation with Newton's equations of compressible fluids on the space of densities.
_source: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Khesin, Misiolek and Modin, 2021

name: Symplectic and Poisson reduction for hydrodynamics
function_signature: (Hamiltonian system with symmetry group) → (Reduced equations + Casimir invariants)
description: Reduction of Hamiltonian systems with semidirect-product symmetry used to derive Hamiltonian/Poisson structures, Casimir invariants, and equations of motion for ideal, barotropic and magneto-hydrodynamic fluids.
_deps: Newton's equations on diffeomorphism groups and density spaces
_source: Geometric hydrodynamics and infinite-dimensional Newton's equations, Khesin, Misiolek and Modin, 2021

name: Frequency envelopes
function_signature: (Data with Littlewood-Paley decomposition) → (Slowly varying dominating sequence tracking energy)
description: A device assigning a slowly varying admissible sequence dominating the Littlewood-Paley pieces of the data, used to track and propagate the dyadic distribution of energy and prove continuous dependence and rough-data well-posedness.
_source: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Ifrim and Tataru, 2023

name: Rough solutions as limits of smooth solutions
function_signature: (Rough data) → (Low-regularity solution with existence, uniqueness, continuous dependence)
description: Constructing low-regularity solutions of quasilinear evolutions by regularizing the data, solving smoothly, and passing to the limit using uniform energy and frequency-envelope bounds.
_source: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Ifrim and Tataru, 2023

name: Quasilinear energy estimates
function_signature: (Symmetrizable hyperbolic system) → (Coercive a priori H^s bound via Lipschitz norm)
description: Coercive a priori bounds for symmetric (or symmetrizable) hyperbolic systems ∂_t u = A_j(u)∂_j u obtained by differentiating, symmetrizing and integrating by parts, controlling the H^s norm via a lower (Lipschitz) norm.
_source: Local well-posedness for quasilinear problems: a primer, Ifrim and Tataru, 2023

name: Convex integration in hydrodynamics
function_signature: (Approximate fluid solution with Reynolds stress error) → (Wild weak solution)
description: An iterative construction adding high-frequency oscillatory perturbations (Mikado/intermittent flows) to approximate solutions of the fluid equations to cancel a Reynolds stress error in the limit, producing wild weak solutions.
_source: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Buckmaster and Vicol, 2021

name: Onsager's conjecture
description: The conjecture that weak solutions of the incompressible Euler equations conserve kinetic energy if their Hölder regularity exponent exceeds 1/3 and may dissipate it below 1/3.
_source: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Buckmaster and Vicol, 2021

name: Resolution of the flexible side of Onsager's conjecture
description: The construction (Isett; Buckmaster-De Lellis-Székelyhidi-Vicol) via convex integration of C^{1/3−} weak solutions of the Euler equations that dissipate energy, proving the sharp threshold predicted by Onsager.
_source: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Buckmaster and Vicol, 2021

name: Nonuniqueness of weak solutions of Navier-Stokes
description: Buckmaster-Vicol's theorem that the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations admit nonunique weak solutions with bounded kinetic energy, obtained by intermittent convex integration.
_source: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Buckmaster and Vicol, 2021

name: Intermittency in convex integration
description: The use of spatially concentrated (high L^∞, low L^p for p<2) building-block flows that mimic turbulent energy concentration and supply the extra integrability needed to dissipate viscosity in Navier-Stokes constructions.
_source: Convex integration constructions in hydrodynamics, Buckmaster and Vicol, 2021

name: Polya-Fourier transform with Gaussian factor
description: The entire function H_{ρ,λ}(z) = ∫ e^{izt} e^{λt²} dρ(t) extending the Riemann ξ-function, whose real-zeros property as λ varies encodes the Riemann Hypothesis.
_source: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type, Newman and Wu, 2019

name: de Bruijn-Newman constant
description: The finite constant Λ_DN ∈ (−∞, 1/2] such that H_{Φ,λ} has only real zeros iff λ ≥ Λ_DN, so the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to Λ_DN ≤ 0.
_source: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type, Newman and Wu, 2019

name: Polya monotonicity / De Bruijn upper bound / Newman lower bound
description: The three facts that the real-zeros set P_Φ is an upper half-line (Pólya), contains 1/2 (De Bruijn), and is bounded below (Newman), which together define Λ_DN.
_source: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type, Newman and Wu, 2019

name: Rodgers-Tao theorem (Λ_DN ≥ 0)
description: The 2018 proof by Rodgers and Tao of Newman's 1976 conjecture that the de Bruijn-Newman constant is nonnegative, formalizing that the Riemann Hypothesis, if true, is only barely so.
_source: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type, Newman and Wu, 2019

name: Newman-Wu weak-convergence theorem for real-zero distributions
description: A theorem that the purely-real-zeros property of Fourier transforms of a sequence of probability measures controls their tail behavior uniformly, used to classify the joint behavior of (T_ρ, P_ρ).
_source: Constants of de Bruijn-Newman type, Newman and Wu, 2019

name: Euler alignment (hydrodynamic alignment) equations
description: The pressure-augmented continuity-momentum system ∂_t ρ + div(ρu) = 0, ∂_t(ρu) + div(ρu⊗u + P) = A(ρ,u) with nonlocal alignment forcing A weighted by a symmetric communication kernel φ.
_source: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023

name: p-alignment hydrodynamics
description: The class of alignment models based on (fractional) weighted 2p-graph Laplacians, generalizing Cucker-Smale alignment to nonlinear p-Laplacian-type interaction operators.
_source: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023

name: Entropic pressure tensor
description: A pressure law required only to form an energy-dissipative process (no thermodynamic closure assumption), introduced to study long-time alignment dynamics with general pressure.
_source: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023

name: Flocking of p-alignment with entropic pressure
description: Tadmor's result that p-alignment hydrodynamics driven by singular (heavy-tailed) communication kernels flock unconditionally even with general entropic pressure tensors and no closure assumption.
_source: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023

name: Energy-fluctuation decay method for flocking
function_signature: (Alignment dynamics with heavy-tailed kernel) → (Quantitative flocking / emergence)
description: Quantifying flocking by controlling the decay of velocity-energy fluctuations, with enstrophy bounds upgraded to Hölder regularity and uniform dispersion bounds, to prove emergence under heavy-tailed kernels.
_deps: Flocking of p-alignment with entropic pressure
_source: Swarming: hydrodynamic alignment with pressure, Eitan Tadmor, 2023

name: Non-Euclidean (incompatible) elasticity
description: The variational model in which a growing thin body carries a prescribed target metric g not realizable by an isometric immersion, and the observed shape minimizes an elastic energy measuring deviation of the realized metric from g.
_source: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis, Lewicka and Mahadevan, 2022

name: Metric frustration as the origin of biological shape
description: The principle that morphogenesis of thin tissues results from differential growth inducing an incompatible (e.g. hyperbolic) metric whose frustrated embedding into ℝ³ selects a shape by elastic energy minimization.
_source: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis, Lewicka and Mahadevan, 2022

name: Gamma-convergence hierarchy of thin elastic plate/shell theories
description: The derivation, as thickness tends to zero, of a hierarchy of reduced 2D energies (membrane, von Kármán, bending/Kirchhoff) as Γ-limits of 3D non-Euclidean elastic energies, indexed by the energy scaling exponent.
_source: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis, Lewicka and Mahadevan, 2022

name: Convex-integration construction of low-regularity isometric immersions of prestrained films
function_signature: (Prescribed growth metric) → (C^{1,α} very-weak isometric immersion with energy-scaling)
description: The use of Nash-Kuiper-type convex integration to construct C^{1,α} very-weak (non-Euclidean) isometric immersions realizing prescribed growth metrics, with energy-scaling estimates for the frustrated shapes.
_deps: Metric frustration as the origin of biological shape
_source: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis, Lewicka and Mahadevan, 2022

name: Monge-Ampère constrained energy for weak prestrains
description: The reduced energy governing weakly prestrained thin films whose admissible out-of-plane deflections are constrained by a Monge-Ampère (Gauss-curvature) equation det(D²v) = f.
_deps: Gamma-convergence hierarchy of thin elastic plate/shell theories
_source: Geometry, analysis, and morphogenesis, Lewicka and Mahadevan, 2022

name: Boolean / Gaussian noise stability
description: The probability that two ρ-correlated random inputs (on the discrete cube or, in the Gaussian limit, on ℝ^n) yield the same output of a function, the central quantity in probabilistic social choice.
_source: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Majority is Stablest theorem
description: Among low-influence balanced Boolean functions, weighted majority maximizes noise stability, with optimal value given by Borell's Gaussian (arccos) noise-stability bound (Mossel, O'Donnell, Oleszkiewicz).
_source: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Quantitative Arrow theorem
description: A quantitative version of Arrow's impossibility theorem: any aggregation rule ε-far from every dictatorship produces an irrational (non-transitive) outcome with probability bounded below polynomially in ε.
_source: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Quantitative Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem
description: Any social choice function far from dictatorship has a non-negligible (inverse-polynomial) probability of being manipulable by a random voter, proved via isoperimetric arguments on the rankings graph.
_source: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Invariance principle for low-influence functions
function_signature: (Low-degree low-influence multilinear polynomial) → (Near-equal distribution under Bernoulli and Gaussian inputs)
description: A nonlinear Lindeberg-type theorem showing low-degree, low-influence multilinear polynomials have nearly the same distribution under Bernoulli and Gaussian inputs, reducing discrete voting problems to Gaussian geometry.
_source: Probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Boolean social choice function
description: A function assigning a societal outcome to a profile of voter preferences (e.g. a Boolean function aggregating n voters' binary opinions), the basic object of probabilistic social choice theory.
_source: A probabilistic view of voting, paradoxes, and manipulation, Mossel, 2022

name: Dold's theorem (equivariant map nonexistence)
description: For a finite group G of order >1, if X is n-connected with a free G-action and Y is paracompact of dimension ≤ n with a free G-action, then there is no G-equivariant continuous map X → Y.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Test map / configuration space scheme
function_signature: (Combinatorial mass-partition problem) → (Nonexistence of a G-equivariant map)
description: Reducing a combinatorial mass-partition problem to the nonexistence of a G-equivariant map by parametrizing partitions as a configuration space X and encoding the splitting via a test map to a space Y with a G-action.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Mass partition problem
description: Given a fixed family P of partitions of ℝ^d each into a fixed number of parts and a family H of measures, deciding whether some partition in P splits each measure in a prescribed way.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: General position (point set)
description: A finite set of points in ℝ^d such that no d+1 of them lie on a common hyperplane.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Necklace splitting theorem (Hobby-Rice / Alon)
description: For m absolutely continuous probability measures on ℝ and r thieves, there is a partition using (r−1)m cuts whose pieces can be distributed among r parties so each receives an equal share of every measure.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Moment curve lifting (necklace splitting proof)
function_signature: (Measures on ℝ) → (Cuts via bisecting hyperplane in ℝ^m)
description: Embedding measures on ℝ via the moment curve t ↦ (t, t², ..., t^m) into ℝ^m and applying the Ham Sandwich theorem, so a bisecting hyperplane yields the required cuts.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Grünbaum-Hadwiger-Ramos problem
description: Determining the smallest dimension d for which a single arrangement of k hyperplanes can equipart any given collection of j measures in ℝ^d.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Nandakumar-Ramana-Rao problem
description: Whether any convex body (or measure) in ℝ^d can be partitioned into k convex pieces simultaneously equal in measure and in a prescribed list of d−1 additional continuous functionals (e.g. perimeter).
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Convex equipartition theorem (spicy chicken theorem)
description: For k a prime power, any absolutely continuous probability measure on ℝ^d admits a partition into k convex pieces of equal measure on which any chosen d−1 continuous functionals are also equalized.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Holmsen-Kynčl-Valculescu conjecture
description: A conjecture asserting bounds on partitions of colored point sets into parts each capturing prescribed numbers of points from each color class while respecting a containment/transversal condition.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Center Transversal theorem
description: For any k+1 measures in ℝ^d there exists a k-dimensional affine subspace that is a center transversal: every hyperplane containing it has at least a 1/(d−k+1) fraction of each measure on each side.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Yao-Yao partition theorem
description: A measure in ℝ^d can be partitioned into 2^d convex cones from a common apex, each of equal measure and with bounded directional spread, enabling efficient geometric range searching.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Same-type lemma
description: Given finitely many point sets in general position in ℝ^d, large positive-fraction subsets can be chosen so that every transversal (one point per subset) realizes the same order type.
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: PPA-completeness of discrete Ham Sandwich
description: Computing a discrete ham sandwich cut, with dimension as part of the input, is complete for the complexity class PPA (Polynomial Parity Argument).
_source: A survey of mass partitions, Roldán-Pensado and Soberón, 2022

name: Categorification
function_signature: (Algebraic invariant) → (Categorical object whose decategorification recovers it)
description: Lifting an algebraic invariant to a richer categorical object (homology groups or a category) whose decategorification (Euler characteristic or Grothendieck group) recovers the original invariant.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Reduced Khovanov homology
description: A variant of Khovanov homology defined using a marked point on the link, splitting unreduced homology and refining the invariant.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Functoriality of Khovanov homology under link cobordisms
description: A smooth cobordism between links in ℝ³ × [0,1] induces a (well-defined up to sign) map on Khovanov homology, making it a functor from the link cobordism category.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Lee spectral sequence and Lee homology
description: A deformation of the Khovanov differential yields Lee homology of dimension 2^{#components}, with an induced spectral sequence from Khovanov homology converging to it.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Rasmussen s-invariant
description: An integer s(K) extracted from the adjacent quantum gradings of the two surviving generators on the E_∞ page of the Lee spectral sequence, defining a concordance homomorphism.
_deps: Lee spectral sequence and Lee homology
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Rasmussen's slice-genus bound
description: The s-invariant is a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group and satisfies |s(K)| ≤ 2 g_4(K), giving a combinatorial lower bound on the slice genus.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Combinatorial proof of the Milnor conjecture (torus knots)
description: Rasmussen's s-invariant gives s(T_{p,q}) = 2 g_4(T_{p,q}) = (p−1)(q−1), yielding the first gauge-theory-free proof that the slice genus of the (p,q)-torus knot equals (p−1)(q−1)/2.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Khovanov stable homotopy type (Lipshitz-Sarkar spectrum)
description: A stable homotopy refinement (a spectrum) whose cohomology recovers Khovanov homology, carrying Steenrod operations that strictly strengthen the homological invariant.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Odd Khovanov homology
description: An integral variant of Khovanov homology (Ozsváth-Rasmussen-Szabó) that lifts the Ozsváth-Szabó spectral sequence to ℤ-coefficients and is mutation invariant.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Kronheimer-Mrowka unknot detection
description: Via a spectral sequence from singular-instanton homology to Khovanov homology, if reduced Khovanov homology of K has rank one then K is the unknot.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Symplectic Khovanov homology
description: A Floer-theoretic (Lagrangian intersection) construction of a link invariant via the geometry of nilpotent slices, conjecturally (and in cases provably) isomorphic to combinatorial Khovanov homology.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Spectral sequences from gauge/Floer theories to Khovanov homology
function_signature: (Khovanov homology, gauge/Floer invariant) → (Detection result)
description: A family of spectral sequences from Khovanov homology to instanton, monopole, or Heegaard Floer invariants used to prove detection results in the spirit of unknot detection.
_source: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Khovanov and Lipshitz, 2023

name: Teichmüller curve
description: An algebraic curve V isometrically and holomorphically immersed in the moduli space M_g of genus-g Riemann surfaces with respect to the Teichmüller metric, i.e. a totally geodesic complex curve.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, ω)
description: The group of derivatives of affine automorphisms of a translation surface (X, ω); when it is a lattice in SL_2(ℝ) the surface is a lattice (Veech) surface generating a Teichmüller curve.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Primitive Teichmüller curve
description: A Teichmüller curve in M_g that does not arise by covering constructions from a Teichmüller curve in a moduli space of lower genus.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Optimal dynamics of billiards in lattice polygons
description: Billiards in a polygon whose unfolding generates a lattice surface have optimal dynamics: every trajectory is either periodic or uniformly distributed; in particular this holds for regular polygons.
_deps: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, ω)
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Regular polygons generate primitive Teichmüller curves
description: The translation surface obtained by unfolding billiards in a regular n-gon has a lattice Veech group and generates a primitive Teichmüller curve.
_deps: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, ω)
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Masur's criterion
description: If the Teichmüller geodesic ray generated by (X, ω) does not return to a compact set infinitely often, then its horizontal foliation fails to be uniquely ergodic; conversely recurrence forces unique ergodicity.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Cylinder decomposition and parabolic affine automorphisms
function_signature: (Translation surface with commensurable cylinder moduli) → (Parabolic elements certifying lattice Veech group)
description: Decomposing a translation surface into parallel cylinders with commensurable moduli and applying simultaneous Dehn twists to produce parabolic elements of the Veech group, certifying that it is a lattice.
_deps: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, ω)
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Weierstrass curve W_D (genus 2 classification)
description: For each non-square discriminant D, the locus W_D in M_2 of genus-2 surfaces with a double-zero 1-form whose Jacobian admits real multiplication by the order of discriminant D, an infinite series of primitive Teichmüller curves.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Classification of primitive Teichmüller curves in genus 2
description: Every primitive Teichmüller curve in M_2 is one of the Weierstrass curves W_D (with the decagon example a special case), giving a complete classification in genus 2.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Finiteness of primitive Teichmüller curves in genus 3 outside W_D
description: In M_3 there are only finitely many primitive Teichmüller curves not belonging to the Weierstrass series W_D.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Infinitude of primitive Teichmüller curves in higher genus (open problem)
description: The open question of whether there exist infinitely many primitive Teichmüller curves in M_g for g ≥ 5, where no infinite construction is currently known.
_source: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, McMullen, 2023

name: Slice knot
description: A knot K in S³ that bounds a smoothly embedded disk in the 4-ball B⁴.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Slice genus
description: The minimal genus of a smooth compact oriented connected surface embedded in the 4-ball with boundary K; slice knots are exactly those of slice genus zero.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Knot mutation
description: Excising a tangle from a knot diagram and regluing it after a rotation, relating the Conway knot to the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot and preserving many invariants.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Knot trace X(K)
description: The 4-manifold obtained from the 4-ball by attaching a 0-framed 2-handle along the knot K in S³ = ∂B⁴.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: The Conway knot is not slice
description: Piccirillo's theorem that the Conway knot does not bound a smooth disk in the 4-ball, settling the last sub-13-crossing knot whose sliceness was unknown.
_deps: Trace invariance of nu (knot Floer slice obstruction)
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Trace embedding lemma
description: A knot K is slice if and only if its trace X(K) embeds smoothly in S⁴, so that sliceness depends only on the diffeomorphism type of the trace.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Handle-rearrangement construction of trace-equivalent knots
function_signature: (Knot K) → (Different knot K' with the same trace)
description: Building the knot trace from a 4-ball plus a 1-handle and two 2-handles and reinterpreting which 2-handle is the attaching knot, producing a different knot K' with the same trace as K.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Trace invariance of nu (knot Floer slice obstruction)
description: The slice obstruction ν from knot Floer homology is an invariant of the knot trace, so knots sharing a trace have equal ν, allowing K' to obstruct sliceness of the Conway knot.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Vanishing of classical slice obstructions for the Conway knot
description: Every classical sliceness obstruction (Alexander polynomial, signature, Rasmussen s-invariant, etc.) vanishes for the Conway knot, motivating Piccirillo's trace-based approach.
_source: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022

name: Topological Helly theorem
description: For a good cover (a family of open sets in ℝ^d all of whose nonempty intersections are contractible), if every d+1 sets intersect then all sets have a common point.
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Colorful Caratheodory theorem
description: Given d+1 color classes in ℝ^d each whose convex hull contains a point x, there is a rainbow selection of one point from each class whose convex hull contains x (Bárány 1982).
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Upper bound theorem for convex sets
description: Bounds the number of k-fold intersection points of n convex sets in ℝ^d in which no d+r+1 sets have a common point, in terms of the number of empty intersections (Kalai 1984, Eckhoff 1985).
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Topological Tverberg conjecture
description: Conjecture that for any continuous map from the (d+1)(r−1)-simplex to ℝ^d there exist r pairwise vertex-disjoint faces whose images have a common point; true for r a prime power and disproved by Frick for general r.
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Sierksma's conjecture
description: Conjecture that the number of Tverberg r-partitions of any (r−1)(d+1)+1 points in general position in ℝ^d is at least ((r−1)!)^d.
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Cascade conjecture
description: Kalai's conjecture that if Σ_i (1+dim T_i(A)) over i=1..r−1 is less than |A| then the r-fold Tverberg set T_r(A) is nonempty, interpolating between Radon and Tverberg.
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Nerve complex method
function_signature: (Family of sets) → (Helly-type bound via nerve topology)
description: Encoding the intersection pattern of a family of sets as a simplicial complex (the nerve) whose combinatorial-topological properties (d-collapsibility, being d-Leray) drive Helly-type bounds.
_source: Helly-type problems, Bárány and Kalai, 2022

name: Impagliazzo-Wigderson theorem (hardness vs randomness)
description: If some problem in E requires Boolean circuits of size 2^{Ω(n)}, then P = BPP, i.e. randomized polynomial time can be fully derandomized.
_deps: hardness amplification (Yao XOR lemma / direct product)
_source: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Hardness amplification (Yao XOR lemma / direct product)
function_signature: (Mildly average-case-hard function) → (Extremely average-case-hard function)
description: Converting a function mildly hard on average into one extremely hard on average by taking XORs or direct products of independent instances.
_source: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Zig-zag product of graphs
description: A graph product (Reingold-Vadhan-Wigderson) combining a large graph with a small one to produce expanders of controlled degree, yielding an iterative combinatorial construction of expander families.
_source: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: SL = L theorem (Reingold)
description: Undirected s-t connectivity can be decided in deterministic logarithmic space (symmetric logspace equals logspace), proved via the zig-zag product.
_source: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Operator scaling / noncommutative optimization
function_signature: (Tuple of matrices) → (Doubly balanced form; null-cone / PIT decision)
description: A geodesically-convex alternating-minimization algorithm over symmetric (group-orbit) spaces that scales tuples of matrices toward doubly balanced form, solving null-cone and noncommutative singularity problems and instances of polynomial identity testing.
_deps: First fundamental theorem of invariant theory
_source: On the works of Avi Wigderson, 2023

name: Efficiency gap
description: A scalar measure of partisan advantage in a districting plan equal to the normalized difference between the two parties' total wasted votes (votes for losers plus surplus votes for winners).
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: Partisan symmetry
description: The criterion that a districting plan's seats-votes curve be invariant under swapping the two parties' roles, i.e. symmetric under (x,y) ↦ (1−x,1−y).
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: Ensemble (outlier) analysis of districting plans
function_signature: (Enacted plan, random sample of valid plans) → (Outlier / gerrymander verdict)
description: Detecting partisan gerrymanders by generating a large random sample of legally valid districting plans and testing whether an enacted plan is a statistical outlier relative to that ensemble.
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: Recombination (ReCom) Markov chain
description: A Markov chain on balanced graph partitions that merges two adjacent districts, samples a uniform spanning tree of the union, and splits it along an edge into two balanced connected parts, mixing far faster than single-unit flip walks.
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: Chikina-Frieze-Pegden local outlier test
description: For a reversible Markov chain, a rigorous statistical significance bound on a plan being an outlier obtained from short random walks without knowing the mixing time, with false-positive probability at most 2√ε.
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: NP-hardness of balanced connected graph partition
description: Sampling or counting balanced partitions of a weighted planar graph into connected pieces of equal weight is NP-hard, even into two parts, formalizing the computational difficulty of districting.
_source: Geometry, Inference, Complexity, and Democracy, Ellenberg, 2021

name: Sunflower conjecture
description: Conjecture of Erdős and Rado that for each r there is a constant c(r) such that any family of more than c(r)^w sets of size at most w contains an r-sunflower.
_source: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Spread (robust sunflower) family
description: A weighted set family is r-spread if for every set T the total weight of members containing T is at most r^{−|T|} of the whole, a pseudorandomness condition forcing the family to look uniformly spread out.
_source: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Kahn-Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture (Park-Pham theorem)
description: For any monotone property, the threshold probability is at most a logarithmic factor times the expectation threshold (the fractional lower bound), proved by Park and Pham via spread families.
_source: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Random restriction with spreadness
function_signature: (Spread set family) → (Forced sunflower)
description: Repeatedly applying random restrictions to a spread set family, shrinking set sizes while preserving approximate spreadness until a sunflower is forced, with Janson-type inequalities at the base case.
_source: Sunflowers: from soil to oil, Anup Rao, 2023

name: Chow ring of a matroid
description: A graded commutative ring built from the flats of a matroid (via the Bergman fan / order complex) that plays the role of the cohomology of a smooth projective variety even for nonrealizable matroids.
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Kahler package for matroids
description: The Chow ring of any matroid satisfies Poincaré duality, the hard Lefschetz theorem, and the Hodge-Riemann relations, despite the absence of an underlying variety (Adiprasito-Huh-Katz).
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Heron-Rota-Welsh conjecture (theorem)
description: The coefficients of the reduced characteristic polynomial of any matroid form a log-concave sequence, proved via the Hodge-Riemann relations on the Chow ring.
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Dowling-Wilson top-heavy theorem
description: For any matroid the number of flats of rank k is at most the number of flats of corank k for k below half the rank (Braden-Huh-Matherne-Proudfoot-Wang).
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Mason's log-concavity conjecture (theorem)
description: The numbers of independent sets of each size in a matroid form an (ultra) log-concave sequence, established via the Hodge-theoretic / Lorentzian polynomial framework (Adiprasito-Huh-Katz, Anari et al., Brändén-Huh).
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Hodge-Riemann relations (combinatorial use)
function_signature: (Degree-graded ring with bilinear form) → (Log-concavity / top-heaviness inequalities)
description: Establishing inequalities by proving that a bilinear form on a degree-graded ring is nondegenerate with prescribed signature, transferring algebraic positivity to combinatorial sequences.
_source: Essence of independence: Hodge theory of matroids, Christopher Eur, 2023

name: Classical verification of quantum computation
description: A protocol in which a polynomial-time classical verifier interacts with a single untrusted quantum prover and accepts only if the prover correctly performs a claimed quantum computation (the BQP verification problem).
_source: Verifying quantum computations at scale, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Trapdoor claw-free function family
description: A family of two-to-one functions for which finding a colliding pair (a claw) is computationally hard while a secret trapdoor allows inversion, instantiated from the learning-with-errors assumption.
_source: Verifying quantum computations at scale, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Mahadev's classical verification theorem
description: Assuming the quantum hardness of learning with errors, there is an interactive protocol by which a classical verifier can verify the output of an arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computation performed by a single quantum prover.
_source: Verifying quantum computations at scale, Thomas Vidick, 2020

name: Cryptographic measurement protocol (qubit commitment)
function_signature: (Quantum prover) → (Committed qubit + verified basis measurement)
description: A cryptographic primitive forcing a quantum prover to commit to a qubit and later reveal a measurement in a verifier-chosen basis, so the prover cannot cheat across bases, built from trapdoor claw-free functions.
_source: Verifying quantum computations at scale, Thomas Vidick, 2020
